units.title: Pulse-versus-JVP Indicators, Arterial Pulse Introduction, Waveform Letters and Pulse Apex Deficit
units.sec: Pulse-versus-JVP Indicators, Arterial Pulse Introduction, Waveform Letters and Pulse Apex Deficit
units.guide:
Pulse indicates left-sided ejection while JVP indicates right-sided filling (p364). The arterial pulse is a pressure wave originating in the aorta d/t LV systolic ejection, travelling at 5 m/s (faster than the 50 cm/s blood column); it indicates LV performance and the vascular reaction, with character/contour best felt at carotids.
Waveform: P percussion (SV/LV contraction), T tidal (aortic recoil), D dicrotic (reflected wave from PVR), DN dicrotic notch (S2). LV markers: ↑ SV gives sharper upstroke + higher peak; ↑ ejection velocity sharper upstroke + earlier peak. Pulse apex deficit: supine, neck turned to palpation side, carotid palpated while auscultating; > 10 means atrial fibrillation.

units.title: Brachiofemoral Delay, Coarctation Captions, Central-to-Periphery Changes and Assessment Features
units.sec: Brachiofemoral Delay, Coarctation Captions, Central-to-Periphery Changes and Assessment Features
units.guide:
Normal delays: carotid 30 ms, brachial 60 ms, radial 80 ms, femoral 75 ms; exaggerated delay = coarctation of aorta, whose captions are LVH on ECG, 3 sign on CXR, coarctation in cardiac MRI and serrated flow on continuous wave doppler (p365). Central→periphery: upstrokes steeper; ↓ peripheral resistance smooths the dicrotic notch and makes the dicrotic wave less prominent.
Assessment features: rate, rhythm, volume, character, vessel wall, peripheral pulses, radiofemoral delay.

units.title: Rate: Tachycardia and Bradycardia Causes, Myxedema and Cushing Notes, Relative Bradycardia
units.sec: Rate: Tachycardia and Bradycardia Causes, Myxedema and Cushing Notes, Relative Bradycardia
units.guide:
Sinus tachycardia: fever (infection), anxiety, exercise, high output states, hypovolemia, myocarditis, anterior wall MI, cardiac tamponade, cardiogenic shock. Sinus bradycardia: athletes, β blockers/CCB, ↑ ICT, hypothermia, inferior wall MI, myxedema (p366). Myxedema coma = unconscious, altered sensorium, bradycardia, hypothermia; Cushing's reflex = ↑ ICT + bradycardia + hypertension.
Relative bradycardia: HR rise not corresponding to temperature (10 beats/min per 1°; 101°F→100, 102°F→110, 103°F→120); infectious typhoid/Q fever/Legionella, non-infectious drug fever/lymphoma/CNS lesions/factitious fever; rule out heart block and β blockers/CCB; dengue, malaria, leptospirosis usually do not cause it.

units.title: Rhythm Tree, Hyperkinetic Pulse Notes and the Collapsing-versus-Pseudocollapsing Table
units.sec: Rhythm Tree, Hyperkinetic Pulse Notes and the Collapsing-versus-Pseudocollapsing Table
units.guide:
Rhythm: regular rapid = SVT/VT; irregularly irregular = AF, atrial flutter, SVT with varying conduction; regularly irregular = VPCs (p367). Hyperkinetic = high amplitude/volume with ↑ SV → ↑ CO; elderly rigid vessel means SV does not increase yet volume is high d/t non-distensibility; ↓ PVR makes the dicrotic wave less prominent; complete heart block has ↓ CO but ↑ amplitude (CO = SV ↑ × HR ↓).
Collapsing (Corrigan's/water hammer): rapid up/downstroke, ill sustained peak, high volume, from two-outlet conditions (AR, aortic sinus rupture, aorto-pulmonary window, PDA); pseudocollapsing: well sustained apex (as printed), normal volume, seen in MR.

units.title: Hypokinetic Pulse, Pulsus Tardus versus Parvus et Tardus and the Bisferiens-versus-Dicroticus Table
units.sec: Hypokinetic Pulse, Pulsus Tardus versus Parvus et Tardus and the Bisferiens-versus-Dicroticus Table
units.guide:
Hypokinetic = ↓ amplitude → ↓ SV (LV dysfunction); pulsus tardus reaches desired amplitude in time (severe AS) while parvus et tardus does not (very severe AS) (p368). Bisferiens = 2 systolic peaks (severe AR with P = T and T > P, AR with mild AS, HCM with P > T); mechanism: AR ↑ SV → large amplitude wave with P & T prominent; AS+AR ↑ turbulent velocity → ↓ lateral aortic pressure (venturi); HCM → SAM; palpation radial preferred.
Dicroticus = 1 systolic + 1 diastolic peak in LV failure (LVF → ↓ CO → ↑ PR); tracing panel prints QS2 = 280, LVET = 190, PEP = 90.

units.title: Alternans versus Bigeminus, Post-Extrasystole Pulse Volume, Pulsus Paradoxus and Its Reverse
units.sec: Alternans versus Bigeminus, Post-Extrasystole Pulse Volume, Pulsus Paradoxus and Its Reverse
units.guide:
Alternans = alternating high & low volume (alternating SV) with fluctuating Ca2+ uptake/release, rhythm regular; bigeminus = normal beat alternating with premature contractions (PMB SV diminished → pause → ↑ filling → ↑ next volume), rhythm regularly irregular (p369). Post-extra-systole pulse volume separates MVP (↑: ↑ filling → ↑ SV → ↑ SBP/volume) from HCM (↓, Brockenbrough sign: ↑ gradient/worsen SAM → ↓ CO/volume, ↑ murmur duration & intensity).
Pulsus paradoxus = systolic BP fall >10 mmHg in inspiration: tamponade, 1/3rd CCP, COPD, PE, SVC obstruction; femoral pulse for palpation. Reverse paradoxus (SBP ↑ with inspiration): IPPV in LV failure, isorhythmic AV dissociation, HCM.
